title: Influences, repertoire and reading in the Celestin band
summary: She had no particular influence. The band played popular music, then arranged music as a 14-piece reading band, and she improvised in solos.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Who do you remember as being one of your early influences on the piano? Can you remember anybody that you...
No, I just liked it. I didn't particularly take, you know, having one as an ideal. I just liked piano, liked music.
What kind of stuff would you have to play to the band, I mean, with Celestan's band? Just...

Well, we played, when we first started out, it was popular music. And then when we went into a large band, which was 14 pieces, then we played only arrangements. Strictly reading, all reading musicians. It was wonderful. We had a lovely large band.
What, even like the drums and the bass, they would all be reading too?
Oh, everybody was reading. We had to because we had special arrangements. We had writers in the band. Who was writing for the band. Yeah. And we had a wonderful society orchestra.
I mean, when you first joined the band, did they, did you just play the way you'd been playing, or did they want to change anything in your playing?

Well, I can't recall, but I knew I was playing music at that time. And I imagine I played... I always could improvise. So I imagine I was improvising then. But of course, it's a little different now because it's New Orleans Jazz. At that time, I think it was more music. Hmm.
I mean, you'd make four pieces of the measure mostly? Yeah, something like that.
And then of course when I would take solos, well then I would improvise. Yeah.
I see. Did you do any writing for the band? No, we had writers.
I didn't do any writing at all.
